title: MV First Person MV Raycast Plugin Development

posts.author: EnergySpike
posts.body:
I'm currently working on a First Person MV Raycast Plugin for RPG Maker MV. While there currently exists some fantastic 3D plugins, I wanted to create something that put more emphasis and control into the First Person side of things. I wanted to create a purpose-made First Person plugin that could be used for a variety of different gameplay styles.
Development is still ongoing as there are still some performance issues that need to be addressed.
I'll be posting a video link to a demo of a General Adventuring type of gameplay below, but I will also note that I will be making several demos as I progress through the Plugin Development. Some other types of gameplay that I'll be creating supporting plugins for using the FPMV Raycast plugin as its core will include:
Horror - This will make more use of lighting, flashlight use, and more.
Dynamic Action - This will primarily be including First Person combat, such as sword play, spellcasting, and even gunplay later on. My focus on this will be to try and create a plugin in such a way where you can create your own Doom-style or Wolfenstein-3D style game, though I'll try to make it as encompassing as I can for different styles of development. The Dynamic Combat will be intended to act as an alternative combat method aside from the built-in turn-based combat system, rather than being a replacement so that both options can be used if needed.
Multiplayer - I absolutely want to create a multiplayer adaption with this setup. I'm currently debating on how I'll be working to set this up, however.
More Pending... - This is primarily driven by whatever I can come up with. If I think of something new to add, I'll typically work toward trying to add it in.
A quick note: I only own RPG Maker MV and do not have access to MZ or any other versions. That's why at this moment I'm only creating this plugin for MV. That may change in the future once I can get my hands on MZ. Additionally, the only plugins in my Demo that are used are the standard Community_Basic for resolution changes, and my FPMV Plugin.
================================================================
Update (June/13/2026):
I've created an
Itch io Page
for where I'll release the plugin. I'm also using the Itch io page to allow people to download the Demo's that I create to showcase the Plugin(s). The Horror Demo has been released, if anyone would like to try it out. It's cheesy, silly, and made very quickly, so there's no coherent story, super scary images, or anything of the sort.

Yeah, I added a Plugin Option to adjust player camera height in case some folks wanted to use the taller sprites.
Edit: I should also note that player movement speed can also be adjusted, as well as either disabling the Sprint option, or changing Sprint to a Quick Dash. I'll be using the Dash more in an upcoming demo for the Dynamic Action demo that I'm planning once I get everything working.

I'm glad it's piqued your interest! I'm hoping to get the core of FPMV out soon. Unfortunately, my best estimation is a within a wide range between 1 week to maybe a few months (primarily depending on my RL situation). There are a few performance issues that I'm currently hunting down, and I'm also trying to build the compatibility for future plugins so that folks won't have to constantly update.
Just to give a bit of insight in my development process, I try to make playable demos (even if its for myself in the short term) with the theme that I have in mind so that I can try and cover all of the bases that I can. It helps me figure out if there's something critical that I've missed. Currently, the next demo that I'm working on is horror-inspired.
I currently have lighting and flashlights working (both with battery usage or infinite battery life). The main thing I want to add for the Horror side of things is a smart enemy pathfinding system, as well as maybe some sound effect options for NPC's walking and player walking. There currently exists directional+proximity-based audio, but I'll be focusing a lot on audio customizations, since audio can sometimes make an average horror game into a masterpiece.
